svg.title: Choking action card for an adult or child aged one year or older
svg.desc: Working Australian choking card for a responsive adult or child aged one year or older. An effective cough is encouraged and watched. For an ineffective cough, call Triple Zero, lean the person forward, give up to five back blows while checking after each, then up to five chest thrusts on the lower half of the breastbone while checking after each. Alternate only while the person remains responsive and blocked. The actions are the same with or without a first-aid kit and equipment must not delay treatment. If the object clears, stop and use the second card's after-clear warning. Abdominal thrusts and blind finger sweeps are prohibited. Infant and collapse actions are on the second card.
svg.text: CHOKING — ADULT OR CHILD AGE 1+
Australian back-blow and chest-thrust sequence
WARNING — HANDS-ON REVIEW OUTSTANDING
Subjective estimates: source match 95%; new illustration 60%.
These are not safety, treatment-success or survival probabilities.
Body and hand positions need accredited first-aid review and practice.
Follow the 000 call-taker. This is not a substitute for training.
Infant under 1 year, or any person collapses? Use Card 2.
CAN THEY COUGH EFFECTIVELY?
Air is moving and the cough is strong: encourage coughing.
Stay with them and watch continuously. Do not strike them.
Call 000 if it does not clear or the cough becomes weak or silent.
INEFFECTIVE COUGH — ACT NOW
Little or no air; weak or silent cough; cannot speak or breathe;
gasping, no sound or rapid deterioration.
Do not wait for blue skin or collapse.
Use Steps 1–3 while the person remains responsive.
CALL 000
Send a named helper if one is present.
Put the call on speaker where possible. Start treatment now.
LEAN WELL FORWARD — BACK BLOWS
Use the heel of your hand
between the shoulder blades.
Give up to 5 sharp back blows.
Check after every blow.
Stop as soon as the object clears.
TARGET: BETWEEN
SHOULDER BLADES
STILL BLOCKED — CHEST THRUSTS
Support the middle back.
Place the other hand’s heel
on the lower half of breastbone.
Not the abdomen.
Give up to 5 thrusts.
Slower and sharper than CPR.
Check each. Stop when clear.
HEEL HERE:
LOWER HALF
BREASTBONE
NOT ABDOMEN
STILL BLOCKED AND RESPONSIVE?
Alternate up to 5 back blows and up to 5 chest thrusts.
Check after every action; never automatically complete all five.
Kit or no kit: use the same actions.
Do not delay to fetch equipment.
Clear? Stop. Use Card 2: AFTER IT CLEARS.
No abdominal thrusts. No blind finger sweep.
Collapse → Card 2.
WORKING DRAFT — age 1+ only; use with Card 2 and follow 000
